name: Olidia

lead: Olidia is a PLLA (poly-L-lactic acid) injectable made by the South Korean company PRP Science. Products of this type are placed in the skin by a clinician and are meant to prompt the body to produce its own collagen, so volume and firmness build up gradually over weeks rather than appearing at once.

The company says effects appear after about 4 to 6 weeks and lists uses such as wrinkles and facial volume. Its main published support is a Korean comparison trial with Sculptra, another PLLA filler, which the company says found identical physicochemical and degradation properties. These claims have been reported by the company rather than by independent reviewers.

paras: It is a clinic procedure. The product is supplied as a powder prepared by the practitioner shortly before injection, and the company says preparation takes about 30 minutes so same-day treatment is possible. Distributor listings describe use in areas such as cheeks, temples, jawline and neck. Results are described as gradual and typically assessed over several weeks.

Dermal fillers in general can cause bruising, redness, pain and itching, and less commonly infection, allergic reactions, lumps or scarring, and rarely vascular complications. Regulatory approvals differ by country: the company reports approval from Korea's drug regulator, CE marking for Europe, and certifications in China and Brazil.

angle.text: Olidia is injected by a clinician to stimulate collagen in the skin. People seek treatments of this kind to soften wrinkles and restore volume in areas like the cheeks, temples, jawline and neck, with results building over weeks.

lead: Olidia is a poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) injectable from PRP Science, a Korean filler manufacturer. Retailers and distributors describe it both as a skin booster and as a dermal filler. PLLA products work differently from hyaluronic acid fillers: after injection the particles are broken down into lactic acid, and the body's reaction stimulates fibroblasts to make collagen, so volume builds gradually rather than immediately[1][2].

On January 10, 2022 the company announced exclusive sales agreements in six European countries, and stated that South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety had approved the product in July 2021, making it the second PLLA filler approved in Korea after Sanofi's Sculptra. It also said Olidia was the third PLLA product worldwide with European CE certification and that it held China NMPA certification and Brazil ANVISA approval[1].

For appearance, the product is positioned for wrinkles and volume. The company reports effects after four to six weeks and a trial of 109 nasolabial fold cases at two university hospitals comparing it with Sculptra[1]. These details come from the company's own statements as reported in the press.

paras: PRP Science describes Olidia as built on its polymer technology with PLLA as the active material. The company states that about 80 percent of particles are uniform in size and that preparation takes about 30 minutes[1].

Wikipedia describes PLLA as a biodegradable synthetic material. Once the carrier is absorbed, the particles degrade into lactic acid, and the body treats them as foreign, recruiting macrophages and fibroblasts that form new collagen. Unlike hyaluronic acid, which adds volume immediately, PLLA builds volume gradually[2].

According to the company, approval in Korea came in July 2021, CE certification covers Europe, and Chinese and Brazilian approvals were obtained, with sales contracts in these regions[1]. Wikipedia notes that CE marking confirms production standards but not medical efficacy, and that fillers are regulated as medical devices in the US[2].

For dermal fillers as a class, Wikipedia lists bruising, redness, pain and itching as common, with infection, allergic reactions, lumps or scarring less common, and vascular occlusion as a rare serious complication[2]. No product-specific safety data for Olidia were located.

The company reports a Korean trial of 109 nasolabial fold cases at two university hospitals that compared Olidia with Sculptra and found new tissue formation and identical physicochemical and degradation profiles; the trial is described in press coverage of the company's announcement rather than in a peer-reviewed article located here[1].

timeline.event: Korean regulator approves Olidia, the second PLLA filler approved in Korea, per the company[1].
PRP Science announces exclusive sales agreements in six European countries[1].
